Definition: an earthen vessel; usually (painful) toil; also a pang (whether of body or mind)
BiblicalUsage: ʻEtseb is sorrow — painful toil, the pang of body or mind — and once, an earthen vessel. In sorrow shalt thou bring forth children, God says after the Fall; the blessing of the LORD adds no sorrow with it; and in all labour there is profit. It is the word for the ache that came with the curse, and for the vessel that holds it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻetseb names the sorrow I know by heart: work that wearies, pain that stays, and the ache of a world under the curse. I hold that the blessing of the LORD is the other side — riches without the sorrow.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
